title: Import/Export: exim and the add-ons it superseded
description: From the 2014 importurls and importLogFiles add-ons, through the exim add-on that began in April 2021, to its HAR, URL, log, PCAP, and Automation Framework features.
narrative:
Bringing captured traffic or server logs into ZAP once meant finding the right small add-on for each format. In March 2014 zap-extensions gained an import URLs add-on, and work on ModSecurity log import followed in September 2014. For a tool used mostly by testers working from recorded traffic, one place for every import format probably made the workflow easier to learn.

The exim add-on began in April 2021, and its starting commit has a body reading "Initial add-on with migration of saveraw and savexml." HAR support followed that month. URL and log importers were added in September 2021, and the CHANGELOG lists a 0.0.1 release in December 2021. In February 2022 a cleanup commit removed the older importLogFiles and importurls add-ons, along with two save add-ons that exim had replaced.

In May 2022 core ZAP deprecated URL export menu items that were being moved to exim. In August 2022 the core HAR API endpoints were deprecated, and the exim CHANGELOG for 0.3.0, dated October 2022, lists HAR related API endpoints being migrated from core. A December 2024 commit aimed to discourage third-party add-ons from using HarUtils.

Exim later also took on the Automation Framework (February 2022) and initial PCAP import (May 2024). The latest entry cited, from March 2026, lists "Support for plugable exporters and importers." In 2022 the core export items were marked for moving into exim, and older import and save add-ons were superseded by it. That probably suits users who move data between tools.

chapters.title: Import add-ons from 2014
chapters.text: The zap-extensions commit "Added import URLs add-on" is dated 2014-03-07. "Issue 432 - Import ModSecurity logs" is dated 2014-09-01 and is the first commit touching the importLogFiles code. On 2019-04-03 commits titled "importurls: relocate to its own project" and "importLogFiles: relocate to its own project" move both into their own Gradle projects.

chapters.title: exim begins on 2021-04-09
chapters.text: The commit "exim: Initial Addition" (2021-04-09) has the body "Initial add-on with migration of saveraw and savexml." It adds PopupMenuSaveRawMessage and PopupMenuSaveXmlMessage. "exim: Add HAR functionality" follows on 2021-04-19.

chapters.title: URLs and logs imported, old add-ons removed
chapters.text: "improve:exim: Add importUrls functionality" (2021-09-27) and "improve:exim: Add importLogs functionality" (2021-09-29) add the URL and log importers to exim. The CHANGELOG lists 0.0.1 (2021-12-22) as "First release." On 2022-02-26 the commit "chore: Remove superseded import and save add-ons" removes importLogFiles, importurls, and two save add-ons; its body reads "Remove importLogFIles, importurls, saverawmesave, and savexmlmessage which have been superseded by exim. (Related to issue 6579)"

chapters.title: Core export items and HAR endpoints are deprecated
chapters.text: In zaproxy, "Deprecate and remove use of URL Export menu items being moved to exim" (2022-05-12) says PopupMenuExportContextURLs, PopupMenuExportSelectedURLs, PopupMenuExportURLs, and PopupMenuCopyUrls are deprecated. "deprecate: Core HAR API Endpoints" is dated 2022-08-23, and the exim CHANGELOG for 0.3.0 (2022-10-27) lists "HAR related API endpoints being migrated from core (Issue 6579)." "Deprecate `HarUtils`" (2024-12-06) says "Discourage the use of `HarUtils` by 3rd-party add-ons."

chapters.title: Automation Framework, PCAP, and plugable formats
chapters.text: The commit "Added support for Automation Framework (with GUI)" is dated 2022-02-26, and the 0.1.0 CHANGELOG entry (2022-03-07) lists "Automation Framework (Issue 7078)" and "Promoted to Beta." 0.9.0 (2024-05-07) lists "Initial PCAP import support (Issue 4812)." The commit "exim: Pcap import - simplest HTTP/1.1 case (#5608)" is dated 2024-09-20. 0.13.0 (2025-01-09) lists "Add Automation Framework job to export data (e.g. HAR, URLs)." and "Support for Sites Tree export and prune." 0.18.0 (2026-03-31) lists "Support for plugable exporters and importers."
